Below is a structured 12-week general fitness program tailored for a 58-year-old male, six months post-MI, cleared for moderate-intensity exercise with HR cap ≈ 70% age-predicted max (~115 bpm), no Valsalva, no maximal lifts, full gym access. The plan emphasizes gradual progression, endurance, muscular endurance, and functional/quality-of-life gains while prioritizing safety.

Assumptions and safety notes
- HR target zones: Moderate intensity typically ~40–60% of heart rate reserve (HRR). With age-predicted max ~162 bpm (220 − 58), 70% is ~114–115 bpm. Since you have a cardiology clearance for moderate intensity and a cap at ~115 bpm, monitor heart rate and RPE (perceived exertion) to stay within safe limits.
- RPE guideline: 11–13 on a 6–20 scale (some sessions might use 4–6/10). If symptoms arise (dyspnea, dizziness, chest pain, undue fatigue, palpitations), stop and reassess.
- No Valsalva: Perform breathing during lifts, exhale on exertion, avoid holding breath.
- No max lifts: Use submaximal loads, emphasize form, tempo, and higher time under tension.
- Medical clearance: Ensure ongoing cardiology follow-up and clearance before increasing intensity or volume.

Program overview
- Frequency: 4 training days per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Sat/Sun), alternating upper and lower body emphasis with a cardio/balance day as needed. Each week has 3–4 sessions adjusted to gradually progress.
- Phases: Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and safety; Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Build endurance and strength; Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Improve functional strength and conditioning with longer, slightly higher reps within safety limits.
- Cardio: 3 sessions/week aligning with HR cap; some sessions include intervals but at moderate intensity and low risk. Keep continuous monitoring.
- Resistance training: 2–3 sessions/week, focusing on full-body movements with emphasis on proper form and control. Primarily machines first, then free weights as tolerated.
- Flexibility and balance: 5–10 minutes of mobility and balance work daily; breathing-focused cooldown.

Weeks 1–4: Foundational safety and capacity
Goals: Establish routine, learn technique, stay under HR cap, build comfort with resistance training.

Week 1
- Session A: Cardio + Upper body
  - Cardio: Treadmill brisk walk or stationary bike, 15 minutes, effort to keep HR around 105–115 bpm or RPE 11–12.
  - Circuit (2 rounds, minimal rest):
    - Chest press machine: 2 sets x 12 reps, comfortable weight
    - Lat pulldown machine: 2x12
    - Seated row machine: 2x12
    - Shoulder press machine: 2x12
    - Bicep curl (machine or cable): 2x12
    - Triceps pushdown: 2x12
  - Core: Plank from knees 3 x 20–30 seconds; standing cable anti-rotation 2 x 12 each side
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes gentle cycle or walk; stretch major muscle groups

- Session B: Cardio + Lower body
  - Cardio: 15–20 minutes, steady, HR ≈ 105–115 bpm
  - Circuit (2 rounds):
    - Leg press machine: 2x12
    - Leg extension: 2x12
    - Leg curl: 2x12
    - Seated calf raise: 2x12
  - Balance: single-leg stand 2 x 20–30 seconds each leg (with support as needed)
  - Core: supine hook-lying marching 2 x 20 steps
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes

Weeks 2–4 progression
- Increase cardio to 18–25 minutes with steady moderate effort, staying under 115 bpm.
- Resistance training: add 1 more set per exercise (3x12) once form is solid; add light dumbbells or machine weights as tolerated.
- Introduce light technique cues: tempo 2–0–2 (2 seconds concentric, 0 pause, 2 seconds eccentric) to improve control and safety.

Week 2
- Session A: Upper body circuit, 3x12, lighter loads; add shoulder external rotation work with light band
- Session B: Lower body circuit, 3x12; add glute bridges or hip thrusts 2x12 (bodyweight or light weight)
- Cardio: 2 sessions of 18–22 minutes at HR 105–115 bpm

Week 3
- Session A: Upper body strength endurance (3x12–15, light-moderate)
  - Add incline chest press if comfortable on machine
  - Dumbbell or cable rows 3x12
  - Lateral raises 2x12
- Session B: Lower body and gait/functional
  - Leg press 3x12
  - Seated leg curl 3x12
  - Stationary lunges or step-ups 2–3x10 per leg (no deep knee flexion beyond comfort)
- Cardio: 20–25 minutes continuous or intermittent at HR cap

Week 4
- Deload week: reduce volume by ~20–30% to consolidate gains and prevent overtraining
- Sessions A/B: 2 sets per exercise or keep 3x10–12 with lighter loads
- Cardio: 15–20 minutes at comfortable pace
- Focus: technique, breathing, postural alignment, ROM

Weeks 5–8: Build endurance and safe strength
Goals: More resistance training volume, maintain HR <115, improve mobility, begin basic conditioning.

Week 5
- Session 1 (Upper Body): 
  - Warm-up: 5–8 minutes cardio
  - Chest press machine: 3x12
  - Seated row: 3x12
  - Lat pulldown: 3x12
  - Shoulder press machine: 3x12
  - Bicep curls: 3x12
  - Triceps pushdowns: 3x12
  - Core: dead bug 2x12 per side, side plank 2x15 seconds
- Session 2 (Lower Body):
  - Leg press: 3x12
  - Leg extension: 3x12
  - Leg curl: 3x12
  - Bodyweight or light hip thrusts: 3x12
  - Calf raises: 3x12
  - Balance: single-leg stand 2x30 seconds
- Cardio: 2–3 sessions, 20–30 minutes, stay under 115 bpm

Week 6
- Slightly increase load if technique solid; keep reps 12–15 where appropriate
- Include 1 day of low-impact interval feel: e.g., 1 minute easy, 1 minute power march or cycle, total 10–12 minutes, but monitor HR to avoid spikes.

Week 7
- Focus on controlled tempo: 2–0–2 or 3–0–2 rep scheme
- Add light functional movements: medicine ball or cable wood chops (safe zone, no load beyond ability)
- Cardio: 25–30 minutes moderate pace with HR cap

Week 8
- Deload: reduce volume by 20–30% across the board
- Emphasize mobility, breathing, and posture
- Cardio: 20 minutes easy pace

Weeks 9–12: Functional strength and conditioning with safety
Goals: Increase overall work capacity, maintain HR safety, emphasize movement quality and daily function.

Week 9
- Session A (Upper Body Strength Endurance):
  - Chest press: 3x10–12
  - Seated row: 3x10–12
  - Lat pulldown: 3x10–12
  - Shoulder press: 3x10–12
  - Bicep curl: 3x12
  - Triceps pushdown: 3x12
  - Core: farmer’s carry (light) 2 x 30 seconds
- Session B (Lower Body Strength Endurance):
  - Leg press: 3x12
  - Leg extension: 3x12
  - Leg curl: 3x12
  - Split squat or step-up: 2–3x10 per leg
  - Glute bridge or hip thrust: 3x12
  - Calf raises: 3x12
- Cardio: 2 sessions 25–30 minutes; include one longer cardio day of 30–40 minutes if tolerated

Week 10
- Increase time under tension slightly: slow tempo on main lifts (2–0–3)
- Add gentle circuit training elements: 2 rounds of 4–5 stations with 30–45 seconds each
- Cardio: include one interval session: 1 minute easy, 1 minute moderate, repeat 8–10 cycles, monitor HR

Week 11
- Focus on daily activity integration: carry groceries, stairs, etc. Improve functional strength
- Resistance: maintain 3x10–12 across major lifts, consider small progression if well tolerated
- Cardio: 2–3 sessions, 25–35 minutes; ensure HR remains below cap

Week 12
- Peak week with safe consolidation
- Sessions: full-body workouts, 3x12 per exercise with moderate loads
- Cardio: 30–40 minutes continuous or 2 x 20 minutes split, low-to-moderate intensity

Daily structure example (repeat with variation)
- Warm-up: 5–10 minutes light cardio (treadmill walk, cycle, elliptical) + dynamic mobility
- Main set: 2–3 compound exercises (e.g., leg press, chest press, seated row) + 1–2 accessory moves
- Core and balance: 5–8 minutes
- Cool-down: 5–10 minutes static stretching and breathing work

Exercise selection and considerations
- Start with machines to teach form, then introduce free weights as tolerated.
- Primary compound movements: leg press, leg extension/curl, chest press, seated row, lat pulldown, shoulder press.
- Accessory work: biceps curl, triceps pushdown, external rotation, hip ab/adduction if available, glute bridges.
- Core: planks (from knees if needed), dead bug, side planks, cable anti-rotation.

Intensity and progression guidelines
- Begin with weights that allow 12 reps with good form; RPE 11–13.
- Progress by small increments (2–5% load) every 1–2 weeks if technique remains solid and HR remains under 115 bpm during work sets.
- If HR approaches cap or symptoms occur, reduce weight, rest more, or substitute lower-intensity movement.
- Avoid max lifts; never hold breath during lifts.

Recovery and nutrition recommendations
- Recovery:
  - Sleep: aim for 7–9 hours per night.
  - Day 1–2: Ensure at least one full rest day or very light activity between sessions.
  - Hydration: 2–3 liters daily if tolerable; adjust for climate and sweat.
  - Mobility and breathing: post-workout 5–10 minutes of mobility and diaphragmatic breathing.
- Nutrition (general guidance; adjust for energy needs and medical advice):
  - Protein: ~1.2–1.6 g/kg/day to support recovery and maintenance; spread across meals.
  - Carbohydrates: balanced intake to support energy for workouts; focus on complex carbs around workouts.
  - Fats: healthy fats (monounsaturated and omega-3s) within daily calories.
  - Sodium: as directed by cardiologist; avoid excessive sodium if blood pressure is a concern.
  - Alcohol: limited or avoided; discuss with clinician.
- Cardiac rehab alignment: ensure any changes are discussed with the cardiologist; monitor for any adverse symptoms and keep a log of HR and RPE.

Monitoring and adjustments
- Before each session, check resting HR and BP if available; ensure HR cap during sessions.
- Use symptom diary: chest pain, dizziness, excessive shortness of breath; stop if any red flags appear.
- Regularly review progress with the client; adjust protocols if tolerance improves or if symptoms arise.

Sample weekly schedule (example)
- Monday: Upper Body Training + 20–25 min cardio
- Wednesday: Lower Body Training + 20 min cardio
- Friday: Full-body circuit or cardio-focused session (60 minutes total)
- Sunday: Light activity + mobility work or rest as needed

If you’d like, I can generate a week-by-week, day-by-day detailed plan with exact exercise lists, sets, reps, and progressive loading tailored to the equipment available at your facility and the client’s specific tolerances. I can also adapt the plan to prioritize aerobic capacity, balance, or functional goals (e.g., stair climbing, daily activities) per your preference.
